subject: Interim processing gateway onboarding — request for subprocessor evidence
messages:
From: Marta Kowalska <marta.k@edgegate-cdn.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interim processing gateway onboarding — notice

Hi Lauren,

Quick heads-up: EdgeGate is going to route a small subset of telemetry and proxy traffic through a temporary gateway cluster in Frankfurt (EU) to handle a capacity spike for one of our banking customers (FinBank). This is a scheduled, short-lived change (expected window: 48–72 hours) to relieve latency on their checkout flows.

We wanted to notify Redwood as an upstream customer and offer to provide the subprocessor manifest + a dataflow diagram and encryption details. I don’t anticipate changes to data residency for your tenants beyond transient transit; payloads will still be delivered back to Redwood endpoints.

If you need immediate proof points (encryption in transit, key jurisdiction, retention) I can attach our manifest and a draft dataflow. We can also schedule a 30-minute call with our security engineer if that helps.

– Marta
EdgeGate Operations

P.S. Attachment plan: edgegate_manifest_20260427.csv, edgegate_dataflow_v1.pdf (will send in follow-up)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Marta Kowalska <marta.k@edgegate-cdn.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interim processing gateway onboarding — notice

Marta,

Thanks for the heads-up and for offering the artifacts. A few quick asks from our side so we can clear this with FinBank and our compliance team: 

- Please send the subprocessor manifest (CSV) and the dataflow PDF as you mentioned.
- Confirm whether any payloads will persist on EdgeGate infrastructure beyond 24 hours and, if so, where they are stored and for how long.
- Encryption: confirm TLS versions in use and whether payloads are additionally encrypted at rest while on the gateway (and which KMS is used).
- Jurisdiction of keys (are any keys bound to non-EU jurisdictions for EU traffic?).
- Any SOC2/ISO27001 attestation or recent audit report you can share.
- If you can offer onshore routing (EU-only egress to an EU KMS or an EU-only egress path) for FinBank traffic, flag that — FinBank usually requires onshore fallback for production outages.

We need to get this to FinBank’s security team within the hour if possible. Can you send the artifacts and a short answers doc and I’ll route to our CS/compliance folks immediately. If you’re available, let’s do a 30-min call at 10:30am PT; invite sent once I hear back.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0196
From: Marta Kowalska <marta.k@edgegate-cdn.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interim processing gateway onboarding — notice

Lauren,

Appreciate the quick reply. Attached are the files: edgegate_manifest_20260427.csv and edgegate_dataflow_v1.pdf. Summary answers below (full details in the CSV):

- Persistence: transient caches persist log/telemetry objects for up to 12 hours. No PII is stored on the gateway layer — only anonymized telemetry identifiers and routing metadata.
- Encryption in transit: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; mutual TLS enabled for upstream connections to Redwood where configured.
- Encryption at rest: short-lived cache writes are encrypted using AES-256; keys are managed in EdgeGate’s KMS (primary region: eu-central-1).
- Key jurisdiction: for Frankfurt cluster, KMS tenant is in eu-central-1. No cross-border KMS access for this temporary cluster.
- Audits: we are SOC2 Type II certified; summary attestation is available (we’ve attached a redacted attestation index in the Drive link).
- Onshore routing: we can pin FinBank traffic to an EU-only egress for the duration of the window; that is available and can be turned on immediately.

I’ve also included a direct link to the attestation snapshot in Drive: https://drive.edgegate.com/attestations/edgegate-soc2-2026-redacted.pdf

We’re standing by for a call at 10:30am PT — I’ll accept the invite.

Best,
Marta
EdgeGate — Customer Ops
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Marta Kowalska <marta.k@edgegate-cdn.com>, security@finbank.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Interim processing gateway onboarding — notice

Hi Marta (and FinBank security team),

Thanks for the artifacts and the clear answers — that helps a lot. Quick internal notes and next steps: 

- We reviewed the manifest and dataflow diagram. Given FinBank’s policy, we’ve asked EdgeGate to enable EU-only egress for FinBank traffic for the duration of the window. Marta confirmed that is available.
- Compliance asked for the redacted SOC2 snapshot; Marta provided a Drive link. Legal will request the unredacted attestation under NDA if FinBank requires it.
- Action items for EdgeGate: please confirm in writing that no unredacted customer payloads will be retained beyond the stated 12-hour window and that KMS access for keys used by the Frankfurt cluster is restricted to eu-central-1 personnel/processes.
- Internal: Jon (cc’d) — please flag for FinBank CS and schedule the follow-up call with EdgeGate + FinBank security. Kim (cc’d) — can you add this manifest & dataflow to the FinBank incident packet and attach the Drive attestation link in the portal?

Marta — once we have the written confirmation items above, we’ll mark this as green for the temporary routing and notify FinBank that EdgeGate’s mitigations meet our controls for transient processing. If FinBank wants an NDA and a copy of the full attestation, our legal team (legal@redwood.com) will coordinate.

Appreciate the rapid runway here.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
